subject: Request: temporary temporal lock for halcyon-13b-l6x variant (compat checks & canary)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Simon Park <simon@aureus.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporal lock for halcyon-13b-l6x variant (compat checks & canary)

Hi team,

Following the model intake results from last week, Aureus provided the halcyon-13b-l6x checkpoint. Prod flagged a small but reproducible safety regression on our long-form summarization prompts when served with the default quantization profile. Before we push through any automatic variant selection I want to request a short temporal lock (14 days) so we can run compatibility and runtime checks and stage a controlled canary.

Ask / context:
- Lock request: 14-day temporal lock on coverage-based autopromotion for halcyon-13b-l6x (prevent auto-roll to this variant).
- Why: alignment/safety signal + uncertainty about KV-cache layout and quantization offsets on our runtime. Marcus flagged potential cache key format differences in the checkpoint metadata.
- What we need from infra/runtime: a compatibility signoff for: 1) KV cache serialization across multi-precision runs, 2) attention kernel stability with 1.5x seq lengths, 3) quantization parity versus our baseline (int8->int4 fallback).
- What we need from product/safety: a canary plan and pass/fail metrics (regressions, hallucination delta, latency P95).

Attachments: halcyon-compat-matrix.csv (compat checklist), halcyon-canary-plan.md (initial canary steps). Also linking the intake doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/halcyon-intake

Timeline proposal: begin compatibility tests tomorrow (Mon), run 3 days of harnessed regression tests + 7 day canary on 5% traffic if checks pass. Approve temporal lock today if no objections.

Simon (Aureus) — I cc'd you so the vendor knows we're pausing autopromote while we validate.

Thanks,
Laura
---
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Simon Park <simon@aureus.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporal lock for halcyon-13b-l6x variant (compat checks & canary)

Laura — thanks for the clear ask and the artifacts.

Quick questions before I greenlight the lock:
- Marcus, can you confirm whether the KV-cache difference is purely metadata (version tag) or an actual reordering of cache keys that would break warm starts across variants? If the latter, we may need a short runtime patch or a compatibility shim.
- Stephanie, do you have a preliminary list of the safety/regression thresholds you want us to gate on for autopromotion? Keep in mind the SLA for dedicated customers requires <2% increase in hallucination failure rate to consider safe.

If we can get those answered today, I can approved a 14-day temporal lock scoped to autopromotion-only (does not prevent manual canary deployment). Dylan

Dylan/Laura — digging into the checkpoint metadata and our runtime logs. Short summary:
- The checkpoint uses a custom KV-key prefix ("hx_kv_v2") and stores per-layer dtype hints in a metadata blob that our loader currently ignores. That means our existing KV-reuse path would treat the incoming cache as incompatible unless we either:
  1) add a loader-layer that recognizes the prefix and rewrites keys at load-time (fast but needs unit tests), or
  2) force a cold-start on canary nodes (simpler but increases canary latency and costs).

Technical ask: give us 48 hours to prototype the loader shim and run the compatibility harness. If the shim looks brittle, we'll fall back to cold-start canaries restricted to low-traffic pools. Also watch out — the quant profile on this checkpoint flips a trailing-axis packing that can degrade int4 perf by ~8-12% on our A100 kernels; we should include a perf regression in the canary pass/fail criteria.

Attachments: small patch diff stub referenced in halcyon-compat-matrix.csv.

Marcus
Principal Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks reasonable. From Safety/Product side:
- Pass/fail metrics we want in the canary: hallucination rate (benchmarked on the same prompt set), ROUGE-L delta on summarization, extraction precision on entity tests, latency P95, and a card for customer-facing error rate.
- Hard gates: no increase >2% hallucination and no ROUGE-L drop >1.5 points for the target cohort. If either gate fails we rollback immediately and we require root-cause analysis before any further promotion.
- I support the 14-day temporal lock on autopromotion. We should allow manual, targeted canaries with constrained traffic and cold-start nodes if Marcus needs that route.

Can we also add a lightweight telemetry hook to capture attention score distributions for the sample prompts? That will help us debug the long-form regressions.

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product Safety
Redwood Inference
